title: Revenue per Unit Sold (Safe Division with NULLIF)
description:
For each product, compute the **revenue per unit** (total_revenue / units_sold). Some products have zero units sold — use NULLIF to avoid a division-by-zero error and return NULL instead.

**Table: product_sales**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| product_id | INT |
| product_name | VARCHAR |
| total_revenue | DECIMAL |
| units_sold | INT |

Output columns: `product_name`, `units_sold`, `revenue_per_unit` (rounded to 2 decimal places). Order by `product_name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE product_sales (product_id INT, product_name VARCHAR, total_revenue DECIMAL, units_sold INT); INSERT INTO product_sales VALUES (1,'Laptop',4999.95,5),(2,'Phone',0.00,0),(3,'Desk',1499.95,5),(4,'Chair',0.00,0),(5,'Monitor',699.98,2);
solution_sql: SELECT product_name, units_sold, ROUND(total_revenue / NULLIF(units_sold, 0), 2) AS revenue_per_unit FROM product_sales ORDER BY product_name

test_cases.description: Phone and Chair show NULL; others show computed revenue per unit

hints: NULLIF(value, 0) returns NULL if value equals 0, otherwise returns value.
Dividing by NULL returns NULL — no error.
explanation: `NULLIF(units_sold, 0)` converts zero to NULL. SQL division by NULL returns NULL rather than throwing an error. Products with 5 units: Laptop 4999.95/5 = 999.99, Desk 1499.95/5 = 299.99. Monitor: 699.98/2 = 349.99.
